previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with mast cell activation syndrome, rheumatoid arthritis, and organizing pneumonia was admitted for pneumonia with symptoms of productive cough, fever, and dyspnea. She also reported epigastric pain, nausea, and itching consistent with her usual mast cell flares. A chest CT confirmed improvement in known organizing pneumonia lesions but revealed a new small lung nodule to be followed in six months and incidental low-density splenic lesions requiring outpatient ultrasound. She was treated with azithromycin and cefpodoxime for pneumonia. After multidisciplinary review, IV narcotics and antihistamines were discontinued, and she was managed with oral medications. The team concluded her symptoms did not represent anaphylaxis, and she was advised to develop a formal pain management plan with her pain specialist. She remained stable, required no pain medications by discharge, and was sent home with instructions to complete antibiotics and follow up with her providers.

Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, without mention of hemorrhage

purposefully creating wheezing heard at some points during 
pulmonary exam.  More pointedly, she seemed more distressed by 
the fact that her IV medications were going to be limited.  
During last admission, pt was instructed to follow-up with her 
pain physician, ___, appointment was 
rescheduled.  As such, she did not have a pain plan to present 
to the physicians during this hospitalization.  Pt received IV 
Benadryl overnight to aid with reported puritis, but no IV 
opioids nor IV ativan.  Plan was discussed with her PCP (Dr. 
___, ___ at patient's request overnight, who 
agreed with IV benadryl and IV phenergan overnight, and that no 
IV narcotics or benzodiazapines given no need for them to be 
administered in the setting of a mast cell crisis.  In fact, 
opioid medications have been shown to destabilize mast cells in 
___, and unclear physiologic explanation for why opioids and 
benzodiazepines would help during actual mast cell crisis.  When 
pt was told that she would no longer require IV Benadryl, she 
stated that she might as well go home.  Pt was instructed to 
follow-up with Dr. ___ to draft a pain regimen plan, and 
Dr. ___ other medical conditions.  Continued other 
home medications as follows: methadone, nitrofurantoin, cromolyn 
nasal spray, ranitidine, lorazepam 0.5-1mg PO q6h PRN, and 
hydromorphone 2mg PO q6h PRN.  PLEASE NOTE: THIS PHYSICIAN

INPT PAIN REGIMEN, AND ___. ___ (___) 
REGARDING DRAFTING A MORE OFFICIAL PAIN PLAN.  COPIES OF THIS

TO THE APPROPRIATE PHYSICIANS.

stating that she has a good relationship with her outpt
